proposed_widenings.name: permanent_progression
proposed_widenings.justification: ASI and feat-grant features are applied once at level-up, permanently modifying the character. They have no activation cost, no use-count resource, no reset cadence, and no transient effect — the entire 'activation' family shape is wrong. A new family is needed for permanent character advancement mechanics.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see "Feats") or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

proposed_widenings.name: grant_feat
proposed_widenings.justification: The core mechanic is granting a feat choice (either the ASI feat or another qualifying feat). No existing ClassFeatureEffect covers this. 'grant_proficiency' is unrelated. The v4 effect atom inventory has no atom for feat grants or permanent ability score advancement.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see "Feats") or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

notes: The existing ClassFeatureActivationMechanics family is structurally incompatible: it models in-game activated features with use pools and reset cadences. ASI is a one-time permanent advancement with no activation cost, no resource, and no reset. The TAXONOMY §12 explicitly marks 'modify_ability_score as a runtime effect' as out-of-scope, confirming the gap. All other class ASI features at L4 (barbarian, bard, cleric, fighter, monk, paladin, ranger, rogue, sorcerer, warlock, wizard) share the same structural widening.
